evidence.label: Étale covers with a prescribed exterior sheet

headline: Points on p-adic curves of genus two or more are claimed to match exactly the sections of their fundamental group.
scope: The curves are smooth, proper and of genus at least two, over any finite extension of the p-adic numbers.
plain: Grothendieck predicted in 1983 that, for curves of genus two or more, points can be read off from symmetry groups alone. Each point gives a splitting of a certain group, called a section. The conjecture says every section comes from exactly one point. The second paper claims to prove the local version, over the p-adic numbers. It also claims the global version for some curves over number fields, including the modular curves X₀(N) and X₁(N).
doesNot: This does not prove Grothendieck's global section conjecture for every curve over a number field; that still needs an extra descent condition.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: A. Grothendieck, in his letter to G. Faltings
scorecard.significanceWhy: The local p-adic section conjecture was a central open problem in anabelian geometry, if this proof holds.

explanation:
Take the curve y² = x⁵ + 1. A few points with whole-number coordinates sit on it. For example, (0, 1) works because 1² = 0 + 1. So do (0, −1) and (−1, 0). The right-hand side has degree 5, which gives this curve genus 2. Genus counts the holes in the curve’s complex picture, like the two holes of a double doughnut.

Now change the numbers you allow. The p-adic numbers, for a prime p, measure size by divisibility by p instead of by distance. A curve still has points with p-adic coordinates. The curve also has a fundamental group, written π₁(X) (a group recording how loops and coverings of the curve fit together). It sits over the Galois group of the base field (the symmetries of its numbers). A section is a way to lift each base symmetry into π₁(X), compatibly.

Every point gives a section[1]. Grothendieck’s section conjecture, from his 1983 letter to Faltings, predicts the converse for curves of genus at least two[2]. Every section should come from a point, and different points should give different sections. Then the points could be recovered from groups alone. The local p-adic form asks this over a finite extension of the p-adic numbers[1].

Earlier work came close. Koenigsmann proved a birational version, using a larger Galois group of the curve’s function field[3]. Pop and Stix showed that each section sits at a valuation extending the p-adic one[4]. A valuation here is a way to measure size on the curve’s functions. The open step was passing from such a valuation to an actual point[5].

The second paper claims the local conjecture in full[6]. For every prime p, every finite extension of the p-adic numbers and every such curve, points and sections match one to one[7]. Back on y² = x⁵ + 1 over the 5-adic numbers, each section would mark exactly one 5-adic point.

The key step is a statement about completions of fields of functions. It claims a section at a valuation lifts to the larger Galois group[8]. Then Koenigsmann’s theorem and a classical argument about two valuations finish the case. The geometry is a gluing problem. Near a branch point, a cover can be replaced by a trivial cover and glued back. But that needs roots on every sheet above a ring around the point, not just one[9]. The paper builds those roots in two stages.

The paper also draws a global consequence for curves over number fields[10]. There, the section conjecture follows when a descent condition holds: the descent locus must equal the rational points[10]. Stoll’s criteria give that condition for the modular curves X₀(N) and X₁(N) of genus at least two over the rationals[15,11]. For other curves the condition stays a real extra hypothesis[12]. The first paper builds a related cover with prescribed behavior on small p-adic disks[13].

How sure is this? No Lean formalization is listed for these papers in the openai/math release. So no computer proof checker has checked them. The argument draws on many deep published results in p-adic geometry. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Major only if the proof holds. No Lean formalization is listed and no specialist review is published. The global result needs an extra descent condition, met for the modular curves named.

glossary.meaning: The number of holes in a curve’s complex picture; a double doughnut has genus 2.
A number system for a prime p where a number is small when it is divisible by a high power of p.
A group that records how loops and finite coverings of a curve fit together.
The group of symmetries of a field of numbers that respect addition and multiplication.
A way to lift every symmetry of the base field into the curve’s fundamental group, compatibly.
A rule that measures how large or small the functions on a curve are.
A curve, such as X₀(N), whose points describe elliptic curves with extra level structure.
